preconditions.expression: len(stdin.splitlines()) >= 2 and stdin.splitlines()[0].strip().split() == [T_str, M] and T_str.isdigit() and len(M) == 26 and all(c in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' for c in M) and all(c != d for c in M for d in M if c != d)
preconditions.description: The first line contains an integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 100) and a string M (a permutation of 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz') separated by a single space. T is the number of sentences, and M defines the Bytelandian-to-English mapping for lowercase letters.

preconditions.expression: all(len(s) > 0 and len(s) <= 100 and all(c in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_!?.,' for c in s) for s in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each of the T subsequent lines is a non-empty Bytelandian sentence (length ≤ 100) containing only lowercase letters, uppercase letters, underscores, and punctuation symbols: '.', ',', '!', '?'

postconditions.expression: stdout == '\n'.join([translate_sentence(s, M) for s in stdin.splitlines()[1:]]) + '\n'
postconditions.description: For each Bytelandian sentence S in the input (after the first line), the output is the English translation of S, where each character is translated as follows: (1) lowercase letters are mapped using M (e.g., if M[i] is 'q', then Bytelandian 'a' (index 0) maps to 'q'), (2) uppercase letters are translated by mapping their lowercase counterpart and then capitalizing the result, (3) underscores are replaced with spaces, and (4) punctuation symbols ('.', ',', '!', '?') remain unchanged.
